title: Canonical module-valued Cech-to-cohomology comparison
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal U:X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ an open cover, and $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Form its Cech complex $C^\bullet(\mathcal U,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] in modules over $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ by restricting scalars on each section module. Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The double complex with terms $C^p(\mathcal U,I^q)$ has total complex $T$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], with differential $d_I+(-1)^q d_C$ when resolution degree is the first index. Restrictions of global sections define $\alpha:\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to T$ in Cech degree zero, and the augmentation defines $\beta:C^\bullet(\mathcal U,F)\to T$ in resolution degree zero. Since injective modules are Cech-acyclic, $H^n(\alpha)$ is invertible. Define $c_{\mathcal U,F}^n:H^n(C^\bullet(\mathcal U,F))\to H^n(X,F)$ by $H^n(\beta)$ followed by $H^n(\alpha)^{-1}$ and the injective-resolution identification with module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Equivalently, $c_{\mathcal U,F}^n$ is the map whose composite with the identification $H^n(X,F)\cong H^n(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet))$ and with $H^n(\alpha)$ is $H^n(\beta)$, for every injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$. These are the canonical comparison maps of Stacks 01EQ.
